instruction: Please help me change the color theme of VS Code to Default Dark+.

parameters.command: SETTINGS_PATH="$HOME/.config/Code/User/settings.json"; [ ! -f "$SETTINGS_PATH" ] && echo '{"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' > "$SETTINGS_PATH" || (grep -q "workbench.colorTheme" "$SETTINGS_PATH" && sed -i 's/"workbench.colorTheme": "[^"]*"/"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"/' "$SETTINGS_PATH" || jq '. + {"workbench.colorTheme": "Red"}' "$SETTINGS_PATH" > temp.json && mv temp.json "$SETTINGS_PATH")

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VS Code color theme from 'Red' to 'Default Dark+'. Evaluator checks if settings.json contains the correct theme value. Uses existing compare_config metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses check_json_settings metric which parses settings.json as JSON and checks specific key-value pairs.
The metric correctly extracts expected['expected'] to get the dict {'workbench.colorTheme': 'Default Dark+'} and verifies this setting exists in the file.
Complete coverage: Instruction requires changing theme to 'Default Dark+', evaluator checks workbench.colorTheme == 'Default Dark+'.
Logic is correct: get_vm_file fetches settings.json from VM, check_json_settings parses JSON and verifies the specific setting, allowing other settings to exist.
Expected value is semantically correct: 'Default Dark+' matches the instruction requirement.
